titolo: Putin Vows 'Inevitable' Revenge After Ukraine Hits Refineries and Air Base
angolo: Putin promises retaliation for the refinery campaign while Kyiv says it hit the Savasleyka air base (the Kinzhal jet base) the same day: what is confirmed, what is claimed, and what could come next.
descrizione: Putin Vows 'Inevitable' Revenge After Ukraine Hits Refineries and Air Base. Putin told Russian oil executives that retaliation for Ukrainian refinery strikes is inevitable, and Ukraine's foreign minister answered with two words: stop complaining. The next day Kyiv said it hit Savasleyka air base and damaged five aircraft; Russia had not commented at the time of reporting. Here is what is confirmed, what is only claimed, and what could happen next.
tag: Putin Vows 'Inevitable' Revenge After Ukraine Hits Refineries and Air Base

scene.testo: Five warplanes. Hit on the ground. Deep inside Russia, Ukraine says.
A day earlier, Ukraine reported striking Russian refineries. Russia's oil system was under pressure.
Then Vladimir Putin said Russia would retaliate.
Retaliation, he said, is inevitable. What will Moscow do next?
Ukraine's foreign minister answered with a short reply. You'll hear it in a moment.
First, the room where Putin said it.
It was Tuesday, at a Kremlin meeting with oil executives.
He accused Kyiv of ignoring a direct request from Donald Trump.
In Putin's words:

citazione.testo: The Kiev regime does not stop attacking our oil refining facilities, despite the appeal and direct request of the US president to refrain from these attacks.

scene.testo: Then came the line the world is now repeating.

citazione.testo: I would like to point out that retaliatory actions on our part are inevitable. Everyone should know this.

scene.testo: He did not specify what the response would be.
He also asked for additional security measures at energy facilities.
Why is Moscow so concerned? One number stands out.
Forty-five percent. That is how far Russian refining volumes have fallen since late October, according to two industry sources cited by Reuters.
That's since late October, according to two industry sources cited by Reuters.
Remember that number. It is part of the backdrop to Putin's remarks.
Who is the man making the threat?
Vladimir Putin, president of Russia.
He ordered the full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022.
Today, that war is nearly five years old.

visivo.testo: Today, that war is nearly five years old.

scene.testo: Now its drones have reached targets more than 1,500 kilometers inside Russia, Ukraine's General Staff says.
How did the refinery strikes escalate? Follow the timeline.
September: Trump called on Zelensky to stop targeting Russian refineries, saying the attacks were 'hurting the world', according to CNBC.
Kyiv's stated position: it will halt strikes on Russian energy sites once Moscow stops hitting Ukrainian ones, Al Jazeera reported.
Late October: Ukrainian strikes picked up again, Al Jazeera reports, after easing following Trump's mid-October energy ceasefire declaration.
By one count, Ukrainian strikes have halted all or part of production at 16 Russian refineries in November, according to the Kyiv Post.
Now the map. Here is where the latest strikes were reported.
On the night of November 23, Ukraine's General Staff said it hit the Perm refinery.
And the Kaleykino oil pumping station in Tatarstan, which Ukraine's General Staff also said it hit. Russian regional officials confirmed a strike near Almetyevsk, TASS reported.
The same night, the Novoshakhtinsk refinery in Rostov was struck.
The Rostov governor said it halted operations.
Fires were also reported overnight at the Syzran and Kuibyshev refineries in Samara region, and the governor said more than 145 drones were shot down, the BBC reports.
Zelensky said earlier this month that Ukrainian long-range strikes had disabled more than 55% of Russia's oil-refining capacity, CNBC reports.
That is Kyiv's claim. Industry sources cited by Reuters put the cut in crude processing at 45 percent.
Fuel supply is the pressure point at home.
Putin said the domestic fuel market situation remains difficult.
But he said petrol prices have stabilised after peaking in October.
He called for more refining in Siberia and the Far East.
He called for developing oil refining and petrochemicals in the east of the country.
And a message to the West about oil and gas.
Now, Kyiv's reply.
Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha answered on X on Tuesday.
His post:

citazione.testo: If Putin doesn't like Ukraine's strikes on his oil refineries, he can order an end to the war.

scene.testo: He added: 'Stop complaining.'
He added: if Putin doesn't want his military vessels hit, he can order an end to the war.
Sybiha also said Russia has lost 432,000 soldiers on the battlefield this year.
The Hill said the figure could not be verified.
Kyiv's stated position is consistent: strikes stop when Russia stops hitting Ukrainian energy, Al Jazeera reported.
But has Russia stopped? Look at the last 48 hours.
scene.capitolo: THE OTHER SIDE OF THE GRID

scene.testo: Overnight, Russian strikes hit Ukraine's power sector, Ukrainian officials said.
Outages in five regions: Dnipropetrovsk, Donetsk, Zaporizhzhia, Odesa and Kharkiv.
Zaporizhzhia was in the most difficult situation, Prime Minister Koretskyi said.
The governor said a morning attack on Zaporizhzhia city hit a residential building and injured six, including two children.
The occupied Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant lost external power again.
The 17th time this year, said Ukraine's deputy energy minister.
It switched to diesel generators.
Winter is setting in. The pressure on Ukraine's grid is rising.
So both sides are now hitting each other's energy sector. Each blames the other.

visivo.testo: So both sides are now hitting each other's energy sector. Each blames the other.

scene.testo: Then came Wednesday's twist. Not a refinery. An air base.
Ukraine's General Staff said it struck the Savasleyka air base.
It sits in the Nizhny Novgorod region, about 300 kilometers east of Moscow, the BBC says.
Three MiG-31 jets and two Su-34 fighter-bombers, Kyiv says.
Kyiv says the Su-34s are used in glide-bomb attacks on Ukraine.
Kyiv says MiG-31s from this base carry Kinzhal missiles used against Ukrainian cities. The General Staff did not specify the MiG-31 variant.
The jets will be unable to fly for some time, the General Staff said.
The General Staff said the extent of the damage is still being assessed.
And Russia? It has not commented, the BBC reports.
So the claim is Kyiv's alone for now. It has not been independently confirmed.
So what will Putin do now? He has not said.
Moscow has not said what its response will be.
Ukraine's allies have warned the country faces another winter of blackouts and freezing temperatures, CNBC reports.
Meanwhile Washington's role is unclear. In September, Trump urged Zelensky to stop targeting Russian refineries.
The Trump administration previously threatened to cut off intelligence sharing if Kyiv did not stop its refinery strikes, according to The Hill.
Kyiv's line has not changed: end the war, end the strikes.
Moscow's line: retaliation is inevitable. Two stated positions, no meeting point.
Winter is coming. Ukraine reports refineries hit and grids damaged. Planes sit damaged, Kyiv says.
